--- title: "Week 16" author: "Victoria Sjalim" date: "2026-11-8" format: html execute: freeze: auto --- # Eris pipeline Updates - Re-naming headers for \_cds.fna become 0 index - I also removed any gene, CDS, or protein sequences that not related with IS (update on 1 Oct) `>ISEc23_IS66_unknown_DOWNSTREAM_FGS_228 HG941718.1:236781-238499 strand=-` - I reinstated all the result from pyfgs for IS-CDS relation - Fix the bug to detect 2 IS that was near to each other **Problem: If there were 2 IS that really close together, eris found it as one IS not 2** ![Genome browser](../result/new_pipeline_block/IS_block_problem.png) - Create `synonym.py` - Detect number changes --> Dimas's new code # Eris-validation Updates I made a new validation repo for IS-CDS relations ([eris-validation](https://github.com/Victoriasja18/eris-validation)) How it works can be seen here: ([eris-validation-pipeline](https://victoriasja18.github.io/eris-progress/week_progress/validation_pipeline.html)): # Result ::: {#b4a60c16 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd RESULTS = "../result/eris_validation" ASSEMBLIES = {"complete": "Complete genome (FASTA)", "simulated": "Simulated GFA", "real": "Real-reads GFA"} pd.set_option("display.max_rows", None, "display.max_columns", None, "display.max_colwidth", None) relations = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f"{RESULTS}/EC958/{a}/relations.tsv", sep="\t").assign(assembly=name) for a, name in ASSEMBLIES.items()], ignore_index=True) relations["reason"] = relations["reason"].fillna("–") pd.crosstab([relations["status"], relations["reason"]], relations["assembly"])[list(ASSEMBLIES.values())] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: # FN and FP reasons Each row of `relations.tsv` now has only three statuses (**TP**, **FN**, **FP**) and a separate **reason** for FN and FP, so each reason points at one kind of bug. The reasons are checked in this order: | Status | Reason | Meaning | |---|---|---| | FN | `wrong_side` | its own IS reports the CDS, but only on the other side | | FN | `wrong_IS` | only a differently named IS reports the CDS, on the same side | | FN | `not_found` | not reported at all (see the miss cause below) | | FP | `unplaceable` | eris's nearest gene cannot be placed on the reference | | FP | `wrong_side` | a truth CDS of its IS, but on the other side | | FP | `wrong_IS` | a truth CDS on the same side, but of a differently named IS | | FP | `not_in_truth` | in no truth relation | To make it easier can be seen in this link: ([reason-explanation](https://victoriasja18.github.io/eris-validation/scoring-guide.html#findings)): ## Wrong-IS cases A wrong-IS row only says the gene belongs to another IS's relation. `distance_error` helps judge each case: - **a few bp**: eris's IS sits where the truth IS is, so eris probably **misnamed** the IS (e.g. ISSen10 called IS629, IS26_2 called ISEc9); - **thousands of bp**: a **different IS further away** reports the same gene (e.g. ISEch14 at ~52 kb), which looks like a real neighbouring IS rather than a naming bug. ::: {#63b2fa03 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} wrong_is = relations[relations["reason"] == "wrong_IS"] wrong_is[["assembly", "status", "side", "is_id", "locus_tag", "eris_target", "truth_distance", "eris_distance", "distance_error"]].sort_values(["assembly", "distance_error"]).reset_index(drop=True).fillna("") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: # Miss causes: not called vs not reported The old miss cause `gene` was a catch-all. It is now split, so every FN gets one of three miss causes | Miss cause | Meaning | Where the bug is | |---|---|---| | `budget` | the `--hops 20` run finds it | eris stops walking too early | | `not_reported` | pyfgs **called** a gene that is the truth CDS (same strand, ≥ 50 % overlap), but eris never reports it as a flank of that IS on that side | eris's flank walk / reporting, or the IS (missed or misnamed) | | `not_called` | **no** gene pyfgs called is the truth CDS | gene calling (pyfgs), or a truth CDS that has no real ORF | How it works: the scorer takes **every** gene pyfgs called on the assembly (6,245 on the real-reads GFA), not only the reported ones, and places each on the reference with minimap2, the same way as the flank genes. If any of them matches the truth CDS, the gene was called, so the miss is `not_reported`; otherwise `not_called`. Where the called genes come from changed this week. Since my eris change `0aac337`, `_cds.fna` holds only the reported genes (about 450 per assembly), which made every called-but-unreported gene look `not_called`. The scorer now reads every called gene from eris's `_assembly.gff` instead, cutting each one out of the assembly, so the split is the same as before that change. ::: {#e854cced .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} fn = relations[relations["status"] == "FN"] pd.crosstab([fn["miss_cause"]], fn["assembly"])[list(ASSEMBLIES.values())] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: What the split shows: - **Most GFA misses are `not_reported`** (25 of 34 simulated, 46 of 57 real-reads): pyfgs did call the gene, so the loss is in eris's flank walk and reporting (the collapsed repeat "roundabouts" below) or in the IS itself, not in gene calling. - **`not_called` stays about the same on every assembly** (15 complete, 9 simulated, 11 real-reads), so it is not caused by fragmentation. - **On the complete genome, 12 of the 15 `not_called` truth CDS are pseudogenes** (`pseudo = True`, mostly also partial), often genes broken by the IS itself. They have no intact ORF, so pyfgs cannot call them. The other 3 are tiny genes of 69–144 bp (ykiE, ykgR, a GNAT fragment). So most `not_called` misses come from the truth including pseudogenes, not from a pyfgs bug. ::: {#3b7e1831 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} complete = relations[(relations["assembly"] == ASSEMBLIES["complete"]) & (relations["miss_cause"] == "not_called")] span = complete["truth_location"].str.extract(r":(\d+)-(\d+)").astype(int) complete.assign(length_bp=span[1] - span[0])[["is_id", "side", "locus_tag", "gene", "product", "length_bp", "partial", "pseudo"]].reset_index(drop=True).fillna("") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: # Why the GFA assemblies score worse | Both sides | Complete | Simulated GFA | Real-reads GFA | |---|---|---|---| | F1 (precision / recall) | 0.70 (0.61 / 0.81) | 0.55 (0.48 / 0.64) | 0.50 (0.49 / 0.51) | | Truth relations found | 95 of 117 | 60 of 94 | 60 of 117 | | Correct nearest-flank calls | 76 | 38 | 41 | | False nearest-flank calls | 48 | 41 | 42 | | Distance band agreement | 0.71 | 0.65 | 0.62 | (The simulated GFA is built from the chromosome only, so its truth has 94 relations instead of 117.) The two GFAs lose on both recall and precision, but for one main reason: **collapsed repeats**. The number of false calls is about the same on all three assemblies (41–48). What drops is the number of correct ones, because eris reports fewer flanks around multi-copy IS. ## Recall: genes eris called but never reports Every missed truth relation, put in the first group that fits: ::: {#673d603d .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} reported_groups = relations[relations["status"].isin(["TP", "FP"])].groupby("assembly")["group"].agg(set) MISS = ["Gene called, but no IS reports it as a flank", "Gene not called by pyfgs", "Reported next to a differently named IS", "Reported on the wrong side", "Only found with --hops 20", "No locus of this IS group has a flank"] def miss(row): if row["reason"] == "wrong_side": return MISS[3] if row["reason"] == "wrong_IS": return MISS[2] if row["miss_cause"] == "budget": return MISS[4] if row["group"] not in reported_groups.get(row["assembly"], set()): return MISS[5] return MISS[1] if row["miss_cause"] == "not_called" else MISS[0] fn = relations[relations["status"] == "FN"] why = pd.Categorical(fn.apply(miss, axis=1), categories=MISS, ordered=True) pd.crosstab(pd.Series(why, index=fn.index, name="why missed"), fn["assembly"], dropna=False)[list(ASSEMBLIES.values())] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}

why missed

Reported next to a differently named IS 1 5 11
Reported on the wrong side 2 2 1

``` ::: ::: - **The biggest group only exists on the GFAs**: pyfgs called the gene, but no IS reports it as a flank (16 simulated, 32 real-reads, 0 complete). `--hops 20` does not recover any of them, so the hops budget is not the problem. - **`Gene not called by pyfgs` is about the same everywhere** (15, 9, 11). On the complete genome these are mostly pseudogenes (see above), so this is not a GFA problem. - **Differently named IS** grows on the real-reads GFA (11, against 1 on the complete genome). These are the wrong-IS cases above: 6 of the 11 are more than 1 kb from the eris locus, genes that a far-away locus such as ISEch14 passes on its graph walk. - **No locus of the IS group has a flank**: ISSen1 on all three assemblies, and ISSen10 on the complete genome, so their relations can't be found at all. Why the called genes are not reported: on a GFA, every copy of a multi-copy IS assembles into **one collapsed contig**, with the unique flanking contigs hanging off it like a roundabout. eris then reports one locus for several copies, and its copy number says how many: ::: {#106906e7 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} def loci(a): report = pd.read_csv(f"{RESULTS}/EC958/{a}/eris/h3_report.tsv", sep="\t").drop_duplicates("locus_id") return report.assign(copy_number=pd.to_numeric(report["copy_number"], errors="coerce")) pd.DataFrame({name: {"loci": len(l := loci(a)), "loci standing for 2+ copies": int((l["copy_number"] > 1).sum()), "IS copies all loci stand for": int(l["copy_number"].sum())} for a, name in ASSEMBLIES.items()}) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}
Complete genome (FASTA) Simulated GFA Real-reads GFA
loci 62 36 36
loci standing for 2+ copies 0 10 13
IS copies all loci stand for 62 51 66
``` ::: ::: On the real-reads GFA, 36 loci stand for 66 IS copies; 13 of them are collapsed, for example IS26 (one locus for 9 copies), IS1A (5), ISEc12 (4) and ISEc23 (4). Nearly all the called-but-unreported genes belong to an IS that has such a collapsed locus: ::: {#f6b2d1a6 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} rows = [] for a, name in list(ASSEMBLIES.items())[1:]: copies = loci(a).set_index("locus_id")["copy_number"] assembly = relations[relations["assembly"] == name] collapsed = set(assembly.loc[assembly["eris_locus"].map(copies).gt(1), "group"]) lost = fn[(fn["assembly"] == name) & (fn.apply(miss, axis=1) == MISS[0])] rows.append({"assembly": name, "called but not reported": len(lost), "of an IS with a collapsed locus": int(lost["group"].isin(collapsed).sum())}) pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("assembly") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}
called but not reported of an IS with a collapsed locus
assembly
Simulated GFA 16 15
Real-reads GFA 32 30
``` ::: ::: So the collapsed locus gets one set of flanks, but the truth has a different flanking gene for each copy. The flanks of the other copies sit on contigs one link away from the repeat, and eris's flank walk in collapse mode does not report them. This is where most of the recall goes, and it points at the flank walk and branch reporting in collapse mode rather than at gene calling or the hops budget. ## Precision: small ORFs, on every assembly ::: {#186f4ec1 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} fp = relations[relations["status"] == "FP"].copy() span = fp["eris_gene"].str.rsplit("_", n=2, expand=True) fp["length_bp"] = span[2].astype(float) - span[1].astype(float) kind = pd.Series("250 bp or longer", index=fp.index) kind[fp["length_bp"] < 250] = "shorter than 250 bp" kind[fp["reason"] == "unplaceable"] = "unplaceable" pd.crosstab(kind.rename("false nearest-flank call"), fp["assembly"])[list(ASSEMBLIES.values())] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ```{=html}
assembly Complete genome (FASTA) Simulated GFA Real-reads GFA
false nearest-flank call
250 bp or longer 19 14 12
shorter than 250 bp 29 23 21
unplaceable 0 4 9
``` ::: ::: - **Most false calls are genes shorter than 250 bp** (29 of 48 complete, 23 of 41 simulated, 21 of 42 real-reads): small ORFs that pyfgs calls between the IS and the real neighbouring gene, so they become eris's nearest flank. This happens on the complete genome too, so it is a gene-calling / filtering issue, not a GFA one. A minimum gene length for flanks could remove most of them, but a few true flanks are this short too (ykiE is 69 bp). - **Unplaceable genes only appear on the GFAs** (4 simulated, 9 real-reads): fragments cut at contig ends that can't be aligned to the reference. - Precision is lower on the GFAs mainly because there are fewer correct nearest-flank calls (38 and 41 against 76), not because there are more false ones.
